title: Longest Happy Prefix
statement: Call a string a *happy prefix* of `s` when it is non-empty, shorter than `s`, and appears both at the start and at the end of `s` (the two copies may overlap). Return the longest happy prefix of `s`, or the empty string `""` when `s` has none.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
notes:
## Intuition

Comparing every proper prefix with the suffix of the same length works, but costs O(n²) on strings like `"aaaa...a"`. The KMP prefix function computes, for every position `i`, the length of the longest border (a proper prefix that is also a suffix) of `s[0..i]`. Its last value is exactly the answer. It builds each value from the previous ones, so the whole table takes linear time.

## Approach

1. Make `lps` of size `s.length` and set `length = 0`, the border length of the part read so far.
2. For each `i` from `1`, try to extend the current border with `s[i]`.
3. While `s[i]` differs from `s[length]`, fall back to the next shorter border, `lps[length - 1]`.
4. If `s[i]` matches `s[length]`, the border grows by one.
5. Store `lps[i] = length`.
6. Return the first `length` characters of `s`.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "level"`. At `i = 1` (`e`) it does not match `s[0] = l`, so `lps[1] = 0`. At `i = 2` (`v`) and `i = 3` (`e`) there is no match either. At `i = 4` (`l`) it matches `s[0]`, so `length = 1`. The answer is `s.slice(0, 1) = "l"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): `length` rises at most once per character, so all the fallbacks together take at most n steps.
- Space: O(n) for `lps`.

## Pitfalls

- The whole string does not count; start `i` at `1` so a border is always shorter than `s`.
- On a mismatch fall back to `lps[length - 1]`, not straight to `0`; `"abacabab"` needs the shorter border `"ab"`.
- The two copies may overlap, as in `"ababab"`, whose answer `"abab"` is longer than half the string.
- Return `""` (not `null`) when there is no border.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `lps` | `lps[i]` is the longest border length of `s[0..i]` |
| `length` | border length of the prefix read so far |
| `i` | index of the character being added |

narration.2: lps[i] will hold the longest proper border length of s up to index i.
narration.3: The border of the one-character prefix is empty.
narration.5: Add the characters one at a time, starting from the second.
narration.6: The next character does not continue the current border...
narration.7: ...so fall back to the next shorter border and try again.
narration.10: So the border grows by one character.
narration.12: Record the border length for this prefix.
narration.14: The border of the whole string is the longest happy prefix.
